sections.heading: C2 — Preparing to drive and driver factors
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Preparing to drive and driver factors

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A03
Fatigued driving can affect a driver in ways similar to alcohol impairment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A03
The handbook compares 18 hours awake with about the driving impairment associated with a .05 percent blood alcohol level. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A03
The handbook compares 24 continuous hours awake with impairment associated with a .10 percent blood alcohol level. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A03
A sufficiently tired driver may fall asleep without realizing it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A03
Even a few seconds asleep at the wheel can be fatal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A03
Teenagers sleeping less than eight hours nightly face increased vehicle-crash risk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A03
If tiredness develops while driving, the handbook recommends stopping driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A03
Vision should be checked every one or two years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A03
Disease and aging can worsen side vision, distance judgment and low-light vision without the driver noticing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A03
Use required glasses or contact lenses every time the vehicle is driven. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A03
Hearing can reveal unseen hazards, approaching emergency vehicles and trains at crossings. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A03
Medical problems, including a stiff neck or sore knee, can interfere with effective vehicle control. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A03
Seizure disorders involving loss of consciousness, diabetes and heart conditions are among the serious driving-related health problems identified by the handbook. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A03
Pennsylvania physicians must report to PennDOT people they diagnose with a condition that could impair safe driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A03
Drivers younger than 21 are considered to be driving under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration of .02 percent or higher. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A03
Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment and memory and impair driving skills. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A03
As blood alcohol rises, driving errors increase while vision, judgment, reactions and vehicle control deteriorate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A03
Alcohol can produce dangerous confidence while reducing the driver's actual skills. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A03
The handbook describes .08 percent as the legal blood alcohol limit for an adult aged 21 or older. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A04
Alcohol in the blood can make driving dangerous even below the legal limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A04
The handbook states that the safe amount of alcohol before driving is zero. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A04
Age, weight, gender, physical condition, food and drugs or medication affect blood alcohol levels. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R23 | anchor: A04
Drinks can contain different amounts of alcohol, so their alcohol content matters. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R24 | anchor: A04
The handbook's standard-drink examples are 1.5 ounces of 80-proof liquor, 12 ounces of regular beer or five ounces of wine. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R25 | anchor: A04
For a person of average weight, the handbook says processing the alcohol in one drink takes at least one hour. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R26 | anchor: A04
The handbook advises legal-age drinkers not to exceed one drink per hour, while warning that this guideline does not work for everyone and does not make driving after drinking safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R27 | anchor: A04
Alcohol is more concentrated in smaller people. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R28 | anchor: A04
A woman may reach a higher blood alcohol level than a same-weight man after equal alcohol intake over the same time. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R29 | anchor: A04
Only time lowers blood alcohol concentration; coffee, other caffeine drinks and cold showers do not reduce it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R30 | anchor: A04
Do not drive after consuming any alcohol, and prevent a person who has been drinking from driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R31 | anchor: A04
Illegal drugs, prescription medicines and over-the-counter products can all impair driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R32 | anchor: A04
Combining drugs with alcohol intensifies side effects and greatly increases crash risk. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R33 | anchor: A04
Marijuana can slow reactions, impair time and distance judgment and reduce coordination. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R34 | anchor: A04
Cocaine or methamphetamine can make a driver aggressive and reckless. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R35 | anchor: A04
Certain sedatives can cause dizziness and drowsiness. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R36 | anchor: A04
Opioids can cause drowsiness and slower reactions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R37 | anchor: A04
Sleeping pills, cough medicines, antihistamines and decongestants can affect driving skills. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R38 | anchor: A04
Read medicine warning labels for side effects before driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R39 | anchor: A04
Ask a doctor or pharmacist about uncertain medication side effects before driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R40 | anchor: A04
A warning against operating heavy machinery applies to driving a vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R41 | anchor: A04
When starting a new medication, consult the doctor and learn its potential side effects. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]
